hints.title: Level Neighbor Linkage
hints.text: Each node in a perfect binary tree must link its next pointer to the node immediately to its right on the same level. Can already established links on one level establish connections on the next level?

hints.title: Parent-Driven Child Linking
hints.text: For any node with children, its left child connects directly to its right child. Furthermore, its right child connects to the left child of the node pointed to by its own next reference.

hints.title: Leftmost Sentinel Level Traversal
hints.text: Maintain a pointer to the leftmost node of the current tier. Traverse horizontally across established next pointers to wire the level beneath, then step down to leftmost.left.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: total number of nodes in perfect binary tree
complexity.notes: Visits each node once using existing next pointers for horizontal traversal without queue allocation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard level-order breadth search using an auxiliary queue consumes O(N) space, violating the constant space constraint.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Reusing previously established next pointers eliminates all auxiliary memory overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Achieving true O(1) extra memory beyond the returned node references.

solutions.approach: Constant-space level linking via parent next pointers
Level traversal using established next pointers
